meta.name: MedRule illustrative knowledge base
meta.note: Educational rules written for a classroom project. Not clinically validated. Review every rule against a trusted medical source before any real use.

common_cold.label: Common cold
advice: Rest and drink plenty of fluids.
Symptoms usually ease within about a week.
common_cold.see_doctor_if: A high temperature lasts more than 3 days, symptoms get worse or do not improve after 10 days, or you feel short of breath or have chest pain.

influenza.label: Influenza (flu)
advice: Rest, stay hydrated and avoid close contact with others.
Monitor your temperature.
influenza.see_doctor_if: You feel very unwell or short of breath, symptoms have not improved after 7 days, or you are 65 or over, pregnant or have a long-term condition. Call emergency services for sudden chest pain, severe breathing difficulty or coughing up blood.

covid19.label: COVID-19 (suspected)
advice: Consider getting tested and limit contact with others.
Rest and stay hydrated.
covid19.see_doctor_if: You are short of breath, have chest pain, a fever lasting 5 or more days, or symptoms that are getting worse. Call emergency services if you are too breathless to speak in short sentences.

allergic_rhinitis.label: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever)
advice: Avoid known triggers such as dust or pollen.
Keep windows closed on high-pollen days.
allergic_rhinitis.see_doctor_if: Symptoms get worse or do not improve with pharmacy treatment.

strep_throat.label: Strep throat (suspected)
advice: A throat swab test is needed to confirm this.
Rest and drink warm fluids.
strep_throat.see_doctor_if: The sore throat has not improved after a week, the temperature is very high, you show signs of dehydration, or the patient is under 5. Go to emergency care if you cannot swallow, are drooling or have trouble breathing.

gastroenteritis.label: Gastroenteritis (stomach bug)
advice: Sip oral rehydration fluids often.
Eat light food once vomiting settles.
gastroenteritis.see_doctor_if: You cannot keep fluids down, vomiting lasts more than 2 days or diarrhoea more than 7 days, you show signs of dehydration, or you see blood. Go to emergency care for blood in vomit, a stiff neck, or sudden severe stomach pain or headache.

migraine.label: Migraine
advice: Rest in a dark, quiet room.
Note possible triggers such as missed meals or poor sleep.
migraine.see_doctor_if: An attack lasts more than 72 hours, the aura lasts more than an hour, or you are pregnant. Go to emergency care for a sudden, extremely painful headache, speech, memory or vision problems, confusion, weakness, or a high temperature with a stiff neck.

dengue.label: Dengue fever (suspected)
advice: Get a blood test for confirmation.
Rest, drink plenty of fluids and avoid mosquito bites.
dengue.see_doctor_if: You have severe stomach pain, repeated vomiting, fast breathing, bleeding gums or nose, blood in vomit or stool, or feel extremely weak or restless.

uti.label: Urinary tract infection
advice: Drink plenty of water.
A urine test is the usual way to confirm this.
uti.see_doctor_if: You have a fever or shivering, back or lower-belly pain, or blood in the urine, symptoms do not improve within 48 hours, or you are a man, pregnant, or 65 or over.

pneumonia.label: Pneumonia (suspected)
advice: See a doctor promptly: a chest examination or X-ray is usually needed.
Rest and stay hydrated.
pneumonia.see_doctor_if: You feel short of breath, have chest pain, or cough up yellow or green phlegm. Seek emergency care if you are struggling to breathe, your lips look blue, or you cough up blood or become confused.

rules.why: at least one head or nerve symptom
runny nose with sneezing is typical of a cold
high fever is unusual for a simple cold
breathlessness is not a normal part of a cold
chest pain is not a normal part of a cold
airway symptoms together with fever and body-wide symptoms
sudden high fever with body aches
loss of smell or taste is a distinctive sign
sneezing with itchy eyes points to allergy
allergy does not normally cause fever
body aches are not typical of allergy
sore throat with swollen neck glands
cough and runny nose suggest a viral cause instead
a visual aura before the headache
fever is not part of a migraine
high fever with pain behind the eyes
headache, body aches and fever together
cold-like symptoms are less typical of dengue
lower belly pain with urinary symptoms
